Maître Boulanger of Autonomous Software

I make software that keeps working while nobody is looking: bots, agents, watchers, phone apps, and the tools that bake them.

Open today: the Atelier’s site, its source, Deckhand’s launch page.

See the shelf @LeSplooch on GitHub

What the title claims

Three words, each answered by work you can read about below.

Since 2019 the record is one long loop: find something that annoys, bake the first loaf quickly, then make it sturdy. It began as Rust tools for Windows and Discord, grew through C# and Kotlin into desktop companions and Android apps, and has lately turned to agents, to a Rust-to-WebAssembly image pipeline, and to the skills that steer an agent in the first place.

What repeats is everything after the first version: the installer, the self-updater, the signing step, the privacy policy, the check that refuses to build when something is off. Most recent work is made in pair with AI coding agents, and the commit history says so.

Maître

Mastery in the old guild sense: not one lane but the whole shop. Seven years on the record, six languages, five surfaces, and the same habit of finishing in all of them.

How the work is made

What repeats from one project to the next, whatever the language.

  1. The model may only subtract

    In the trading terminals a language model can veto a decision or shrink it, never enlarge it, and a deterministic gate has the last word. The Play Store tool lets an agent act unattended on the lowest-stakes track only, in code, with tests that say so.

    • Vireo
    • Kairos
    • Soldream
    • playctl

  2. Ship the installer too

    An MSI and an updater that finds its own releases, a release script that refuses a bad build, a feed the app polls. A program is not done when it runs; it is done when it can arrive and leave.

    • TBaguette’s Mess
    • Hotaru House
    • Deckhand site & feeds
    • playctl

  3. Procedural before pre-made

    One app draws every sprite and synthesises every sound at runtime, and its release script fails if an image or an audio file sneaks in. A browser game scores twenty worlds with synthesised music. Maths first, assets last.

    • Hotaru House
    • Flappy Bunny

  4. Say it in a tiny language

    A clan-tag animator with its own four-word script language; a terminal message player with eighteen directives. When a tool needs scripting, give it a grammar.

    • Clan Tag GIF
    • Animessage

  5. Fail loudly

    A build that stops on a malformed changelog, a site checked by script before it ships, a screen that fails closed on a missing number, a dry-run flag on anything that touches the filesystem. Quiet failure is the expensive kind.

    • TBaguette’s Atelier
    • Deckhand site & feeds
    • Vireo
    • Animessage

Agents in the kitchen 2025–2026

Phone apps, a Rust-to-WebAssembly pipeline, a procedural world, a keyboard, trading terminals with fences, and a library of skills for the agents that now bake alongside.

  1. Sep 2026

    Vireo

    A desktop terminal that paper-trades on-chain tokens, where a language model may veto a trade but never make one.

    Agents & AI · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Rust
    • TypeScript
    • Tauri
    • AI agents
    • Guardrails for models
    • Market data
    How it’s made
    1. A Rust workspace of eight crates under a Tauri desktop shell and a plain TypeScript interface.
    2. Candidates pass a fourteen-rule screen that fails closed when a metric is missing or not a number, then a scoring ensemble, an optional model review, sizing and portfolio limits.
    3. Real trading is structurally impossible: only a paper executor is wired in, a dependency policy and a test ban the signing libraries, and arming anything takes four separate gates.
    4. It brings its own market simulator and a calibration harness that compares runs on paired seeds.

    Kept Sep 2026.

  2. Sep–Oct 2026

    TBaguette’s Atelier

    A hundred and one skills that tell an AI coding agent how to work, and the site, graph and build that publish them.

    Agents & AI · Public · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Python
    • JavaScript
    • AI agents
    • Automation
    How it’s made

    This site is part of it, and so is the page you are on.

    1. 101 skills in 12 families, each project-, stack- and language-agnostic, installable across a dozen agent harnesses.
    2. The showcase site is generated: a build reads every skill and writes the pages, the search and the cross-reference graph.
    3. The graph is a canvas app that draws every place one skill names another, and a check refuses to publish it if it no longer matches the skills.
    4. A changelog parser stops the build when its shape or order breaks, and a test suite gates every change.

    Kept Sep–Oct 2026.

  3. Sep 2026

    TKeyboard

    An Android keyboard with eleven animated skins, glide typing, and a trick for typing on a computer whose layout isn’t your phone’s.

    Phones · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Kotlin
    • Android
    • Jetpack Compose
    How it’s made
    1. Glide typing resamples the finger’s path and every candidate word’s key path to forty points, then ranks by mean distance, endpoint error, length mismatch and word frequency.
    2. A layout transmitter turns each character into the key presses that type it on the host’s layout, handling AltGr and dead keys, so a remote desktop receives what was meant.
    3. Eleven skins, twenty-four bundled dictionaries and an emoji set ship inside the app, built with Jetpack Compose.

    Kept Sep 2026.

  4. Sep 2026

    Hermes Pocket

    An Android app that watches and steers an AI agent running on your computer, over an encrypted relay.

    Agents & AI · Private repository

    • Kotlin
    • Rust
    • Python
    • Android
    • Jetpack Compose
    • AI agents
    • Encryption & signing
    How it’s made

    Its relay is Hotaru House’s.

    1. Chat with streamed answers, tool traces and approvals; a run inbox; a workspace with files and a terminal; and screens for automations and skills.
    2. Records are sealed with AES-256-GCM across a two-party relay that was reused from another of these projects, with its provenance checksummed.
    3. The host-side bridge adds the agent’s API key itself, so the phone never holds it; pairing material sits in the Android keystore.

    Kept Sep 2026.

  6. Aug–Sep 2026

    Hotaru House

    A private, two-person pixel-art world for Android, with end-to-end encrypted sync over a relay written and hosted by hand.

    Phones · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Kotlin
    • Rust
    • Android
    • Encryption & signing
    • Procedural audio & art
    • Installers & updaters
    How it’s made
    1. Every sprite and every sound is generated at runtime; the release script fails if the APK contains an image, an audio file or a font.
    2. The synthesiser is written from scratch: band-limited oscillators, plucked strings, bells, envelopes, a resonant filter and a stereo room.
    3. Records are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a fresh nonce each; a Rust server builds four binaries: a relay, an update server, an append-only archive that only ever sees ciphertext, and an admin tool.
    4. Sync is offline-first with an outbox, and the two phones find each other on the local network.

    Kept Aug–Sep 2026. Spans the app and its release repository.

  7. Aug–Sep 2026

    Deckhand site & feeds

    The animated launch page for a phone-as-control-surface app, with the update feed and notice feed it serves.

    Web · Public

    • JavaScript
    • Browser
    • Scroll-driven motion
    • Installers & updaters
    How it’s made

    Built for Day Dream Corp’s Deckhand; the app is in closed testing.

    1. A chapter engine pins and scrubs scroll timelines, and falls back to calm static layouts for readers who ask for less motion and for short screens.
    2. The page renders the app’s own control decks, fourteen kinds of control you can operate right there.

  8. Aug 2026

    playctl

    A command-line tool that publishes Android apps to Google Play, with limits on what an agent may do unattended enforced in code.

    Agents & AI · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Python
    • Android
    • Automation
    • AI agents
    • Guardrails for models
    • Installers & updaters
    How it’s made
    1. Four tiers of action: automatic, confirm, refresh and blocked. Only the internal track runs unattended; unknown actions ask; blocked ones cannot be confirmed, and tests assert it.
    2. Each edit is a transaction: validate before commit, discard on error, never retry a commit.
    3. Version codes derive from the clock, so build age can be computed, and an unattended refresh may only re-upload the commit already live.

    Kept Aug 2026.

  9. Aug 2026

    Kairos

    A desktop agent that scans a market-data feed and decides with a local model, inside hard risk gates, paper first.

    Agents & AI · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Kotlin
    • Jetpack Compose
    • AI agents
    • Guardrails for models
    • Market data
    • Encryption & signing
    How it’s made
    1. Kotlin and Compose Desktop, in five Gradle modules.
    2. A hand-written API client signs every request and was checked against the vendor’s own reference signer; a leaky bucket and a global cooldown keep it polite.
    3. A local model answers in a fixed schema and can only subtract: veto, or shrink the size.
    4. Going live needs three independent keys; there is a kill switch and a daily-loss breaker.

    Kept Aug 2026.

  10. Jul–Sep 2026

    Soldream

    A desktop trading terminal where a council of model personas proposes and a deterministic risk module decides.

    Agents & AI · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • Rust
    • TypeScript
    • Tauri
    • React
    • AI agents
    • Guardrails for models
    • Market data
    • Encryption & signing
    How it’s made
    1. A Rust and Tauri core with a React interface; every entry a model proposes must pass the risk module before anything is sent.
    2. Designed so a sent trade is never sent twice, and so that keys live in an encrypted vault backed by the operating system’s keyring.
    3. Strategies are drafted by a model and promoted from paper to a trial to live only on a statistical lower bound; so far all of them are still in dry-run.
    4. Knowledge can sync, opt-in and signed, through a small relay written in Rust and hosted at home.

    Kept Jul–Sep 2026.

  11. Jul 2026

    Flappy Bunny

    A one-file browser game with twenty worlds, eight power-up fruits and a leaderboard, and not one image or audio file.

    Web · Private repository

    • JavaScript
    • Browser
    • Procedural audio & art
    How it’s made
    1. The bunny is drawn procedurally with squash and stretch; there are no sprites.
    2. Each of the twenty worlds has its own palette and its own synthesised Web Audio soundtrack, in its own tempo.
    3. The loop is fixed-timestep at sixty hertz, so physics doesn’t care how fast the screen refreshes.
    4. Scores are kept in the browser and on a dependency-free Node server’s top-ten board.

    Kept Jul 2026.

    AudioGem

    An Android utility that makes Bluetooth headphones use the audio codec and quality you picked, and estimates how loud a day of it was.

    Phones · Private repository

    • Kotlin
    • Android
    • Jetpack Compose
    How it’s made
    1. Reaches Android’s hidden Bluetooth codec API through reflection, with fallbacks for how the framework’s constructors changed across versions.
    2. Sets codec, sample rate, bit depth and LDAC quality, and keeps them set from a foreground service.
    3. A listening-dose estimate compares volume and time against a safe-listening table.

    Kept Jul 2026.

  14. Dec 2025 – Jun 2026

    PhotoShield

    A mobile app that stamps photos with invisible marks, with the pixel work done in Rust compiled to WebAssembly.

    Phones · Private repository · Built in pair with AI coding agents

    • TypeScript
    • Rust
    • WebAssembly
    • Android
    How it’s made

    Its privacy policy names Day Dream Corp as publisher.

    Desktop · Private repository

    How it’s made

    A rewrite of the 2023 C# sketch below it.

    1. A Compose Multiplatform desktop app, packaged as an MSI.
    2. The server browser polls a community stats feed about every ten seconds, pings every server at once, and sorts them into tiers.

  6. Jul 2021 – Mar 2022

    Clan Tag GIF

    A Windows tool that animates a player’s clan tag in a game, driven by a script language it parses itself.

    Desktop · Private repository

    • Rust
    • Windows
    • Little languages
    • Automation
    How it’s made
    1. The script language has four words: Show, Wait, Loop and KeyboardLayout. The parser compiles a script in a few milliseconds and warns about code after an endless loop.
    2. It types into the game’s console through synthesised keystrokes, with QWERTY and AZERTY layouts, and pauses whenever the game loses focus.

  7. May 2021 – Apr 2022

    Badass Bot

    A Discord bot, in Rust, that plays each member’s chosen six-second clip when they join or leave a voice channel.

    Bots · Private repository

    • Rust
    • Discord
    How it’s made
    1. Voice-state events feed a per-server queue that a background loop drains, streaming each clip and seeking to a saved start.
    2. A member sets their clip in a direct-message dialogue with timeouts and cancel; only a link and an offset are stored.
    3. State is saved every eight seconds by writing a new file and renaming it over the old, and the process restarts itself after an error.
    4. Two hundred and fifty commits across eleven months.

    Kept May 2021 – Apr 2022.

    A pop-up translator for the desktop, opened by a global hotkey.

    Desktop · Private repository

    The oldest loaf on the shelf, and a prototype.

  2. Jul–Sep 2019

    Watchcord

    A Windows tool, with a French console, that makes Discord use less of the processor so the game gets more.

    Desktop · Private repository

    • Rust
    • Windows
    • Automation
    How it’s made
    1. Every two and a half seconds it finds Discord’s processes and lowers their priority.
    2. It limits them to about a third of the logical processors, building the affinity mask itself.
    3. A release exists, and a self-updater was written, then set aside.

    Kept Jul–Sep 2019.
